title: Controller probes now dry-run EC2 — broken IAM, DNS or networking makes the controller fail its probes

detection.reason: whether the controller can reach and authenticate to the EC2 API is decided at runtime

quote: **Installation of the EBS CSI Driver on clusters with broken networking/DNS, incorrectly configured IAM, or other issues preventing access to the AWS API may fail.**
remediation: Before upgrading, confirm the controller can call ec2:DescribeAvailabilityZones: its IAM role (IRSA or Pod Identity) allows it, and its pods resolve and reach the EC2 endpoint (VPC endpoint or NAT). From v1.49 the readiness and liveness probes perform that call, so a controller that 'worked' while failing AWS calls now crash-loops and the upgrade does not complete.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/ebs-csi-controller -c ebs-plugin --tail=200 | grep -iE 'UnauthorizedOperation|AccessDenied|no such host|i/o timeout'  # any line printed is an AWS API failure the v1.49 probes will turn into a crash loop
coversNotes: URGENT (1.49.0): Add dry-run EC2 API call to ebs-csi-driver controller readiness/liveness probes

title: New XFS volumes may not mount on Amazon Linux 2 nodes (xfsprogs nrext64) — set legacyXFS

detection.reason: StorageClass fstype is not collected yet (Storage tab slice); the hint names the Amazon Linux 2 nodes

quote: **As a result, newly formatted XFS volumes may fail to mount on nodes with older kernel versions.**
remediation: On clusters whose nodes run Amazon Linux 2 (or another kernel older than 5.10) and whose StorageClasses use csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype: xfs, set legacy XFS formatting before upgrading — EKS add-on node.legacyXFS=true / Helm node.legacyXFS / flag --legacy-xfs on the node plugin (v1.49.1+, and from v1.49.1 it also disables nrext64). Otherwise new XFS volumes are formatted with nrext64 and fail to mount on those nodes. Moving the nodes to AL2023 removes the need.
verifyCommand: kubectl get storageclass -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.provisioner == "ebs.csi.aws.com") | "\(.metadata.name): \(.parameters // {} | to_entries | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(" "))"'  # fstype=xfs (csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype) on a cluster with Amazon Linux 2 nodes needs legacyXFS
coversNotes: URGENT (1.49.0): A workaround is available in v1.49.1/v1.50.1 and later.
URGENT (1.49.1): This can be worked around via the --legacy-xfs and node.legacyXFS parameters, see the full
Setting legacyXFS to true now disables nrext64.
